review_notes: I read the whole target file, plus point_at and its use in LevelHeavy.lean, the definition of Data.heavyFlag and Data.point in LevelMap.lean, and every use of heavyFlag_at and point_at in the repo (only the two rewrites in this file and one in LevelHeavy.lean). There are no simp attributes in the file. The main issue is that the two canonical evaluation lemmas, point_at and heavyFlag_at, are not simp lemmas, so each proof does its own manual rw/change. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour. The proposed lemma is a safe orientation: it has no loop risk, and the right-hand side is a strictly simpler atom. I found no cycles or competing simp rules, and the file's other lemmas (heavyEdit_le, heavy_stationary, heavy_mover) are not good simp candidates because their inequalities have hypotheses and bounds.

findings.excerpt: theorem heavyFlag_at (D : Data X N H) (n : Fin N) : D.heavyFlag n.val↔D.heavy n := by
findings.problem: heavyFlag_at is the canonical evaluation rule that turns the ℕ-indexed existential flag `D.heavyFlag n.val` (defined as `∃ ht : t<N, D.heavy ⟨t,ht⟩`) into `D.heavy n` for `n : Fin N`. It is not tagged `@[simp]`, and neither is its companion `point_at` (`D.point n.val = D.center n`). Both are the only normal-form lemmas for these two defs, and the rewrite direction is the right one: the right-hand side is the simpler Fin-indexed atom, so there is no loop risk. Because they are not simp lemmas, every use needs a hand-written `change ... at h` followed by `rw [point_at, dist_comm p, heavyFlag_at] at h` (lines 53 and 68). LevelHeavy.lean line 24 also rebuilds the same fact by hand with `⟨n.isLt,hh⟩`, and line 30 there uses `rw [←he,point_at]`. Any new statement that mentions `D.point n.val` or `D.heavyFlag n.val` will not be normalised by `simp` and needs the same manual rewrites.
findings.proposed_change: Mark both evaluation lemmas as simp lemmas: `@[simp] theorem heavyFlag_at ...`, and `@[simp] theorem point_at` in LevelHeavy.lean. Then `simp only [point_at, heavyFlag_at, dist_comm p] at h`, or a plain `simp` in downstream proofs, normalises `D.point n.val` and `D.heavyFlag n.val`. Replace the manual `⟨n.isLt,hh⟩` construction in LevelHeavy.lean with `heavyFlag_at.mpr hh`. Do not make `heavyTrigger` or `heavyPotential` simp-unfolding: they are not reduced here, and unfolding would expose the large `HeavySchedule.centers` terms.
findings.benefit: The two Fin-indexing conversions would be applied uniformly by simp, so a stated bound over `n : Fin N` reaches the `D.center n` / `D.heavy n` form without ad hoc rewrite lists. This removes the repeated hand-ordered `rw [point_at, ...]` at lines 53 and 68 (and LevelHeavy.lean line 30). It also keeps the competing representations `D.point n.val` / `D.center n` and `D.heavyFlag n.val` / `D.heavy n` from leaking into statements.
